extracted.intended_audience: college mathematics instructors (and teaching assistants) who run homework teams and grade writing/teamwork assignments
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, instructor-facing guidance for forming, running, diagnosing, and evaluating out-of-class homework teams in college mathematics courses, plus related criteria for grading student writing and peer evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism (in student writing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the possibility of plagiarism in several ways: failure to properly reference quoted material; extent of collaboration on team homework and projects; issues arising from word processors where file sharing makes attribution difficult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for unreferenced quotations on reports; be explicit about acceptable extent of collaboration; be aware that word-processed submissions can obscure individual authorship. Instances of blatant large-scale plagiarism are rare but must be guarded against.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency in grading
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain consistency both from student to student on a given assignment and from assignment to assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use procedures that improve reliability (e.g., exemplar papers, checklists, double-marking) to reduce variability in grading; recognize methods can be time-intensive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear introduction (grading checklist, Meier & Rishel)
rubrics_metrics.description: The student has included a clear introduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of a suggested checklist for grading writing assignments—look for an opening that sets up scope and purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear conclusion (grading checklist, Meier & Rishel)
rubrics_metrics.description: The student has included a clear conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the essay ties up its main points and leaves the reader with a coherent takeaway.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization and clarity (grading checklist, Meier & Rishel)
rubrics_metrics.description: The essay is well organized and clear to follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check paragraph flow and global structure so readers can follow the mathematical narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader confusion indicator (grading checklist, Meier & Rishel)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reader has to stop and say, 'Wait! What's going on here?' (negative criterion to avoid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note places where the exposition loses the reader; such moments indicate poor organization or missing explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain purpose of calculations (grading checklist, Meier & Rishel)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a clear indication as to why the student is performing his or her calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mathematical work should be accompanied by explicit commentary about why steps are taken and what they accomplish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of mathematical arguments (grading checklist, Meier & Rishel)
rubrics_metrics.description: The mathematical arguments are clear and well stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess logical structure, correctness, and clarity of proofs/derivations or problem solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph structure supports discussion (grading checklist, Meier & Rishel)
rubrics_metrics.description: The paragraph structure supports the general discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good paragraphing should group related ideas and help the reader follow the argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanics: spelling, grammar, punctuation (grading checklist, Meier & Rishel)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spelling, grammar and punctuation are correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While secondary to mathematical correctness, mechanical errors can impede comprehension and should be noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficulty finding conceptual content (Gopen & Smith)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students may show difficulty finding conceptual rather than factual content in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage assignments and feedback that push students to emphasize concepts and connections rather than rote facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to connect narrative with data (Gopen & Smith)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students often fail to connect narrative exposition with numerical or symbolic data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require explicit linking language and explanation showing how the narrative interprets or uses the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to make connections explicit (Gopen & Smith)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students sometimes do not make important connections explicit in their writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach reader-expectation techniques: state assumptions and rationale so connections are evident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial or suppression of mistakes (Gopen & Smith)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students may deny or suppress mistakes rather than acknowledging and learning from them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use drafts/double submission to allow students to see and correct errors; foster an environment where mistakes are part of learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double submission (revision-based assessment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a double submission system: instructor comments on a first draft; students revise; instructor grades the second version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This encourages improvement in both exposition and understanding; provides formative feedback before final grading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting goal: provide team-formation guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide instructors with guidelines for implementing various strategies for selecting members for homework teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meeting should cover multiple formation strategies and discuss advantages/disadvantages and implementation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting goal: share experienced instructors' lessons
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide experienced instructors with a forum to share important lessons learned in managing homework teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use panels or small-group reports to surface practical tips and pitfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting goal: alert to potential difficulties
rubrics_metrics.description: Alert instructors to potential difficulties with homework teams and initiate discussion on managing these difficulties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Tricky Situations' handouts and facilitated discussion to surface common problems and solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting goal: guidelines for identifying and mediating conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide instructors with guidelines for identifying, confronting, and mediating conflicts between homework team members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss when to intervene, mediation tactics, and what problems the instructor should or should not take responsibility for.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting goal: provide a forum for peer advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide instructors with a forum for hearing others' thoughts on forming/managing teams and related issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage sharing of department-specific practices and identify resource people for follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation: consult experienced instructors
rubrics_metrics.description: If time permits, speak with experienced instructors to gather experiences and focus questions for discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use suggested focus questions (biggest challenges, greatest hurdles, differences between team and individual homework, improvements) to structure the meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation: review and augment team-formation strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the list of strategies for forming homework teams and add new strategies and formation problems specific to your context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate problems of formation vs problems of ongoing teams (reserve latter for 'Diagnosis and Treatment').

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation: review potential problems and create problem/cause/treatment lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the list of potential problems and create department-specific lists using a problem–cause–suggestion-for-treatment format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor interventions to local context and common failure modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation: prepare ice-breakers/focusing activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare ice-breakers (e.g., 'Tricky Situation' sheets) or focusing activities to stimulate discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use brief situational prompts to get participants to identify problems and propose solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation: circulate agenda & materials in advance
rubrics_metrics.description: Circulate the agenda to participants in advance and make copies of meeting materials and questionnaires; confirm attendance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance distribution maximizes productive discussion time and preparedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agenda item: review methods for forming homework teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the merits of different strategies for forming homework teams and allow experienced instructors to share implementation experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider panels or small seeded groups so beginners hear many viewpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agenda item: discuss problems teams experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss common problems homework teams encounter and potential solutions with experienced instructors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use real examples and 'Tricky Situations' handouts to structure discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agenda item: outline instructor responsibilities to teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Outline what kinds of team problems instructors should or should not involve themselves in and strategies for resolving conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify departmental policy and expected level of instructor involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agenda item: ways of measuring team performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss various ways to measure and assess team and individual contributions (e.g., quizzes, peer evaluation forms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider homework quizzes, team evaluation forms, and other mechanisms to verify individual learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outline for running the meeting (timed agenda)
rubrics_metrics.description: A suggested :50 meeting schedule with timed segments: introductions, handout review, panel/small-group discussions, ice-breakers, 'Diagnosis and Treatment' review, team-evaluation form review, wrap-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use panels or seeded small groups, allow time for reflection on handouts, and end with practical 'Hints on How to Make Groups Work'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for team composition (heterogeneous vs homogeneous)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether teams should be heterogeneous or homogeneous according to test scores, race, gender, mathematical experience/background, major or intended career path.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss trade-offs (e.g., heterogeneous ability balances groups vs. potential dominance by strong students; homogeneous interest can improve communication but risk off-topic discussion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Student involvement in group formation
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether students have input into group formation: should they decide team size, fully choose teammates, or have no choice? Consider handling students with no preferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students' choice increases satisfaction but may recreate existing cliques and leave some students hurt; set expectations about combinatorial limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Students' Choice team-formation method
rubrics_metrics.description: Form groups from students' submitted lists of preferred and non-preferred partners (name cards with n liked and m disliked names).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages: students like it; groups tend to work well. Disadvantages: may reconstruct original cliques, some students may feel rejected; implementation requires handling missing cards and imperfect matches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixtures-of-ability grouping (by exam scores)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form teams by distributing students across score strata so each group has a mix of low-to-high exam performers (example algorithm provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages: groups uniform in overall ability. Disadvantages: top students may not work with peers, differences in commitment may cause freeloading or dominance; consider adjustments for gender, race, or living-area imbalances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homogeneity-of-interest grouping
rubrics_metrics.description: Form teams based on common non-mathematical interests (e.g., majors) to provide a communication base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May increase rapport but risks off-topic conversation; use student data sheets/mathematical autobiographies to implement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Living/working-area grouping
rubrics_metrics.description: Form teams based on geographic proximity (campus/town area) to ease meeting logistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eases scheduling and travel; may introduce imbalances in ability/commitment and is less useful when re-forming teams later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment-to-course grouping
rubrics_metrics.description: Group students by assessed attitudes and commitment to the course and group learning (using evaluation forms, observations, and data sheet questions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to minimize mismatched expectations; difficult to measure accurately and attitudes can change after group formation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tricky situations to anticipate when forming teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples to consider: commuters or students with heavy work obligations requesting individual work; teams unable to find common meeting times; high-stakes students requesting individual work; multi-campus students with transit constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have policies for exceptions, consider team size flexibility, and be prepared to reassign or accommodate on a case-by-case basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tricky situations to anticipate when managing teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Common management issues: alleged nonattendance/exclusion; one student doing all write-ups; overqualified students feeling meetings wasteful; non-participating members; synchronized drops from same team; identical submissions by roommates; poor write-up when scribe absent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate with the team, require documentation (reporter), use homework quizzes, rotate roles, and set clear expectations about responsibilities and evidence of contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disease: Group not working together (Diagnosis & Treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Symptoms: reporter or student report that group is not working together; different writing styles; low homework quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treatments include homework quizzes, group evaluations, meeting the group in office hours, discussing schedules to find meeting times, and pointing out that groups who work together perform better.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disease: Atmosphere not conducive to learning (Diagnosis & Treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Symptoms: reporter tells you; students report poor atmosphere; group interaction problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meet with the group (in office), stress appropriate behavior to all members, and emphasize creating an environment supportive of learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disease: Mismatched commitment to course (Diagnosis & Treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Symptoms: some group members attend class and others do not; inconsistent participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss personal and group goals with members; use homework quizzes; consider dropping lowest scores or other assessment techniques; encourage active participation and clarify roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disease: Group works together but not everyone learns (Diagnosis & Treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Symptoms: group homework looks good but some individuals' exam or quiz scores lag; same scribe always writes up; differences seen in quizzes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reassure active learners, emphasize the clarifier role, give individual quizzes based on team homework, and encourage increased individual participation during meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hints on how to make groups work — Things that help
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical behaviors that improve group functioning: know each others' names; have one person read the problem; ensure everyone listens; allow friendly expression of differing opinions; resolve disagreements without fighting; ensure equal involvement; set correct pace; reach consensus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these as ground rules for teams and include them in orientation materials or handouts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hints on how to make groups work — Things to avoid
rubrics_metrics.description: Behaviors to discourage: formation of cliques; leaving anyone out; 'laying back' (not participating); making others feel 'dumb'; one person talking all the time; straying off-topic; rushing before everyone understands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coach teams to recognize and correct these dynamics; intervene when persistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team evaluation: Attendance at group meetings (peer-eval item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate each team member's attendance at group meetings (Not a real strength=0; Okay=1; A real strength=2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used on the Team Evaluation Form to assess contribution; collect mid/term and end-of-term to detect patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team evaluation: Has read the material and tried to work the problems (peer-eval item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate whether the member has read the material and attempted the problems (0/1/2 scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures preparedness; helps detect freeloaders and informs instructor interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team evaluation: Comes to the meetings on time (peer-eval item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate timeliness of attendance at group meetings (0/1/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness affects group efficiency; use as part of summative/ formative evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team evaluation: Helps to keep the group going (peer-eval item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate whether the member helps to sustain group momentum and progress (0/1/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses leadership/contribution to workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team evaluation: Is willing to listen (peer-eval item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate whether the member listens to others (0/1/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures collaborative attitude and respect for peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team evaluation: Puts effort into the process (peer-eval item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate the member's effort devoted to team activities (0/1/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates engagement and work ethic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team evaluation: Is willing to disagree (peer-eval item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate whether the member is willing to disagree constructively (0/1/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructive dissent can improve understanding; encourage respectful debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team evaluation: Knows whether other members understand (peer-eval item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate whether the member monitors peers' understanding (0/1/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A key collaborative skill—helps identify who needs help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team evaluation: Helps assure that everyone understands the solution (peer-eval item)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate whether the member helps ensure group consensus and comprehension (0/1/2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closely tied to the 'clarifier' role; important for equitable learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team evaluation: Describe the group member (qualitative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a descriptive label or brief characterization of the member (examples: Worker, Leader, Leech, Obnoxious Type-A Personality, Sloth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives qualitative context to numeric ratings; can inform role assignments or instructor interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team evaluation: Would you again be in a group with this person? (Y/N)
rubrics_metrics.description: Binary question asking teammates whether they'd choose to work with this person again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful summary indicator of perceived reliability and fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team evaluation: Perception Likert items about group experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual responses to statements: 'Being part of this group helped me understand the material'; 'Meeting with this group was better than working problems on my own'; 'Meeting with this group was a good experience.' (Agree/Neutral/Disagree scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to assess perceived learning and satisfaction; responses can guide whether to continue or modify team structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-eval scoring scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Numeric scale used on Team Evaluation Form: Not a real strength = 0; Okay = 1; A real strength = 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple three-point scale for straightforward peer assessment; combine with qualitative comments and aggregate for instructor decisions.
